Question_text: A student uses the apparatus shown for two electrolysis experiments. Complete the table. Give a test and observation to identify chlorine gas.

Calcium carbonate reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid. A student investigates how the rate of this reaction changes as the temperature increases. State one variable, other than the concentration of the hydrochloric acid and the temperature, that is likely to affect the rate of this reaction. The student is asked to control the temperature of each experiment so that it remains constant for the whole time that the calcium carbonate and dilute hydrochloric acid are reacting. This method does not keep the reaction mixture at constant temperature throughout the experiment. Explain why. Suggest how the method can be improved so that the reaction mixture is at constant temperature throughout the experiment.

A student is provided with three bottles: one contains dilute hydrochloric acid, another contains aqueous sodium sulfite and the third contains aqueous sodium sulfate. For each of the three bottles, describe a test and its positive result to identify the contents of the bottle. Chemical equations are not required.
Unit: UNIT 12: Experimental techniques and chemical analysis

Question_text: A student determines the percentage of iron in a powdered sample of impure iron by a titration method. The student adds the sample of impure iron to a previously weighed beaker which is then reweighed. Calculate the mass of impure iron used in the experiment.

Question_text: The reaction between aqueous lead(II) nitrate and aqueous potassium iodide produces a precipitate of lead(II) iodide. A student has two solutions. The student determines the concentration of G by adding different volumes of H to 4.0cm³ of G in a test-tube. The student uses a burette to measure the volumes of G and H. Why does the student use a burette instead of a measuring cylinder?
